title: Broadcast a chat over axum WebSockets
summary: Turn an echo handler into a chat with split and broadcast, then stop slow clients from being dropped silently on Lagged.

turns.user: /ws just echoes right now. make it a chat, anything someone sends goes to everyone connected. theres already a broadcast sender in AppState

assistant.body: Let's split the socket in two. WebSocket::split gives a SplitSink and a SplitStream, and each can be moved into its own task. The send task reads from a broadcast subscription and writes to this client. The receive task takes text from the client and pushes it into tx. rx.recv only fails once every Sender is dropped, so a while let Ok loop is enough there. When either task finishes, tokio::select! aborts the other one, so nothing is left running after a disconnect.

turns.user: works. but in busy rooms some people just get dropped. nothing in the server logs

assistant.body: Correction: I was wrong about recv only failing on close. A broadcast channel shares one ring buffer, and a receiver that falls more than its capacity behind gets RecvError::Lagged and skips the oldest messages. while let Ok treats that as the end, so the send task returned, select! aborted the receive task, and the connection closed. Lagged now tells the client how many messages it missed and carries on. Only Closed ends the loop.

turns.user: fixed. someone said 16 is way too small, make it 256. also the skip notice looks like a normal message, prefix it with system:

assistant.body: The capacity is set on the one line that creates the channel, and it is how far behind a slow receiver may fall. One sed changes that and the notice text together.
sed -i '' -e 's/broadcast::channel(16)/broadcast::channel(256)/' -e 's/format!("({skipped} messages skipped)")/format!("system: {skipped} messages skipped")/' src/main.rs
